extracted_tips: Basic step rhythm is 'quick, quick, slow' — think of it like a drum beat where every time your foot hits the floor it's a beat.
Pick up your feet with knees up ('up, up, up'). Don't flat-foot or you can't move fast enough for the quick steps.
Every step is a weight change — you take a step and immediately commit your weight so you're ready for the next move.
Partner hand hold: leaders palms UP, followers palms OVER. Never use thumbs — use 2 fingers (middle + ring, like Spider-Man) to cuff around the follower's fingers. Just relax, don't grip.
Right turn footwork: forward, forward, turn to the right. The turn happens on the slow count. Always end on the right foot because footwork is always right, left, right.
Stay on the line when turning right — turn right but don't drift forward off the line. Go right, then come back to center.
After the right turn, immediately go into basic: 'ta-ta-po' (back, back, forward). Full pattern is right turn then basic, repeating.
Leader signals the follower's right turn by lifting/picking up the hand on the second bar. Leader does 3 basics throughout — your forward does not change because you're not turning.
Use only ONE hand for the right turn — left hand holding follower's right. Do not hold with 2 hands. Signal on count 1, the turn happens on counts 2-3.
Hand flip trick during the turn: with the 2-finger Spider-Man grip, flip your wrist back as the follower turns, then flip it back down after. Cuff around her fingers, then release and re-catch.
Spotting during turns: pick a target, keep your eyes on it, bring your head right back to that target after rotation.
Leader's own right turn: forward, forward, turn. Left hand comes down, turn around, fingers rotate behind back, switch hand. Follower just keeps doing her basic.

extracted_tips: Before a left turn, twist your body to the right to prepare. This unlocks you from the right twist into the left twist on count 3.
On count 6, you should be facing forward again after the left turn. Your right leg goes back on 6, not forward—keep your weight centered.
The turn happens on count 3. Your weight shifts and you pivot, but count 7 stays in place—just shift your weight without moving that foot.
Keep your arm styling close to your right ear on counts 1-2-3. Don't let it drift outward; bend it and keep it controlled near your body.
Trace your body with your arm styling from count 5 (behind your neck) through count 7 (down the body) to count 1 (up). Do this with intention, not tentatively.
Cross, step, cross—keep your back foot close behind your front foot. Don't pass your front foot; stay tight and controlled.
When doing Suzy Q, twist your hips for styling. This creates the visual effect of crossing without overextending your legs.
You can prep a Suzy Q by lifting your right leg on counts 5-6-7-1 before starting the cross-step-cross pattern.
After Suzy Q (counts 5-6-7-1-2-3), do quarter beats by stepping only on odd numbers: 1 and 3. These are core beats—just the high numbers.
Count 1-2-3-5-6-7 for a basic step. That's 6 steps total. If you're stepping more, you're losing time and the count.
There's a break between each set of 3 counts: 1-2-3 (break) 5-6-7 (break). Use these breaks to reset and stay on time.
When leading a left turn, twist your arm on count 2 subtly—not exaggerated. Bring your right hand closer to you and your left hand closer to your follow.
Leaders: don't step into your follow's space. Keep a normal step forward but add hip twist on count 2 to signal the left turn.
When leading a left turn, keep your right hand centered and lift your left hand up and out. Don't confuse your follow with mixed signals.
Followers: pivot off your right foot while your left foot swings to the left during a left turn. Keep your right elbow down to maintain frame.
Leaders must be assertive with direction and guide. Use body language and touch to show your follow where to go—don't let them guess.
When turning your follow, keep your arms at shoulder width around their head. Don't use wide arms; stay compact and controlled.
Followers: don't change your basic step when the leader starts going back with their left foot. Keep your normal pattern until the lead signals otherwise.

extracted_tips: Always cross in front of your foot, whether crossing over left or right—never behind. This is the standard for Suzy Q.
Say the pattern aloud as you move: 'cross, step, cross, cross, step, cross.' Saying it helps you execute it correctly.
Pick up your leg after the cross to prepare for the next step—don't drag your foot.
For circular Suzy Q, think of four directions: bathroom, wall, door, and mirror. Turn to face each direction as you complete each Suzy Q repetition.
Create smooth curves and circles rather than sharp corners when transitioning between directions in circular Suzy Q.
You can reverse the circular Suzy Q by starting with your left foot and going to the right instead of left. The mental pattern stays the same.
If you struggle with Suzy Q, practice Suzy Q in isolation before attempting the full combo. Master the basic movement first.
On counts 3 and 7, keep your weight planted and don't move your foot—these are anchor points that stay in place.
Counts 1 and 2 travel forward; count 3 stays in place. Counts 5 and 6 travel back; count 7 stays in place.
If you move your 3 or 7, you'll step on your partner. Keep these anchor points stationary to maintain the connection.
Start turning on count 6, not before. Don't hesitate—commit to the turn at 6.
The follower turns to the right on count 2. As the leader, raise your hand on count 1 to signal the turn, and guide them to the right.
Keep your 7 away from your partner, not toward them. This creates space and prevents stepping on each other.
Don't reach high to grab your partner's hand during a turn. Keep your arm low and grab low to maintain control.
Use your elbows to activate the switch, not your hands. Keep your arm straight and use elbow engagement to signal the hand switch.
Don't present your hand slowly—snatch it. Quick, decisive hand movement prevents the follower from reaching for the wrong hand.
After turning on 6, land on count 8 (a pause), then continue with counts 1, 2, 3. Don't rush the landing.
Maintain right-to-right hand hold throughout the turn and transition. Don't switch back to the original hand position—keep the connection flowing.
Take small steps and stay aware of your surroundings, especially when dancing in lines. Stagger slightly if needed to avoid collisions.
Great dancing is made of connection and simplicity, not complex movements. Practice these fundamentals until they feel smooth and fun.

class_structure.section: Full Combo with Right Turn Integration
class_structure.description: Brought together all elements: circular basic + around the world + anchoring + right turn in full 8-count sequence. Multiple repetitions with music.
Instructor ended class with positive feedback and celebration of student progress.

summary: Class #4 (July 14) focused on mastering foundational movement patterns through repetition and building complex combos from simple elements. The instructor taught circular basic step motion, directional variation (around the world), and the critical concept of anchor points (counts 3 and 7) for stability. The bulk of the class was devoted to drilling the right turn with full 8-count timing (5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5), which was repeated multiple times to build muscle memory. By class end, students had integrated all these elements into a flowing combo sequence with proper timing, control, and positioning.
